transcript.content: Hello, I’m Dr. ____. What brings you in today?

Hello, Doctor. It's so very nice to meet you, and thank you for taking the time to see me today. I hope I'm not taking time away from your more serious patients. 

Um, well, I guess I'm here because... well, I feel like I’m just always up and moving. Even on a quiet day when I really should just be relaxing, I'm sort of bouncing around the house. I'll go from checking my garden club list, and then I'm over digging through my knitting bag, and the next thing I know I'm pulling out old travel papers... usually before I’ve actually finished any one of those things. 

I mean, I like to think it's a blessing to have so much energy and stay so active at my age, right? It keeps me young! But my daughter pointed out that I never seem to settle down, and she thought it might be best if I just came and talked to you about it. Does that make sense, or am I explaining it poorly?
Has this always been how you are, or is this a new change for you?

Oh, goodness, no, it's not really a new change. I think I've always been a bit of a... well, a busy bee, I suppose. 

Even way back in grade school, I remember my teachers telling my mother that I was a very bright little girl—which was so lovely of them to say! But... well, they did also mention that I was a little, um, scattered. I guess I was always misplacing my school papers, and I had a bit of a bad habit of talking out of turn. And, oh, I was always wiggling around in my seat before I'd actually finished my schoolwork. 

I really wasn't trying to be a nuisance to the teachers, I promise! I just had so much spirit and wanted to be involved in everything, you know? I hope that's the kind of background information you were looking for? I just want to make sure I'm answering your questions right.
Have you ever had a period of several days or more when you felt unusually energized or euphoric compared with your normal self?

Oh, my, unusually energized or euphoric? Like... like a manic sort of thing? Oh, no, doctor, no, nothing like that. 

I mean, I have my days where I wake up feeling very cheerful and ready to tackle the world, especially if the sun is shining or I have a nice visit with my grandchildren planned. But it's just normal happiness, you know? Just a good mood. I don't ever get, um, out of control or feel like I don't need sleep for days on end. I always make sure to get my rest, even if I am a bit restless while I'm awake. 

I hope that's a good thing? I certainly wouldn't want you to think I was losing my grip on reality or anything like that. I'm just a little energetic, that's all. Is that the right answer?
Do you often have difficulty sustaining your attention when you need to focus on a task?

Oh, goodness. Well, I suppose... sometimes? But really, it's just normal aging, I'm sure of it. 

I mean, if I'm at a garden club planning meeting, or, you know, reading through the Sunday church bulletin, I start out paying very close attention. I really do try to be involved and respectful. But... well, after a little while, I'll suddenly realize I've sort of drifted off, and I might have missed half of what was just said, or what I was just reading. 

It's not that I don't care about what's going on, I promise! I just get a little sidetracked by my own thoughts, maybe thinking about what I need to make for dinner or a phone call I forgot to make. It's nothing terrible, right? Everyone gets a little daydreamy sometimes, don't they? I hope I'm not making it sound worse than it is... I really do try my best to be a good listener.

final_diagnosis.reason: The interview supports attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder with longstanding symptoms beginning in grade school: chronic motor restlessness, difficulty staying seated, impulsive talking out of turn, distractibility, and difficulty sustaining attention. No history suggests a manic episode or another primary mood disorder. Although the provided candidate list only included F90.9, the symptom pattern is most consistent with childhood-onset ADHD, predominantly inattentive/combined presentation rather than unspecified ADHD.
